svg.text: 43,513 lines of source + 2,437 in the MCP server · 48,497 lines of tests · read-only, single lab, 9 Cisco XRd nodes
how a question arrives — five front doors, every one read-only
composes a diagnosis out of already-parsed facts — never out of device text
closes the loop around an investigation — none of it a dependency descent (diagram 8)
552 · polls Loki, groups by root cause
NO MODEL CALL, EVER — if this layer ever needs one, something above it was designed wrong
the only code in the repository that reads raw device text
checked BEFORE credentials load and BEFORE a socket opens — both files frozen since the pre-build baseline
cisco_xr 10 · cisco_iosxe 5 · juniper_junos 5 approved commands. VERB_ALLOWLIST = {ping, show, traceroute}. There is no run_command(), no config mode, no shell.
netmiko over SSH · one login per device per observation window, not one per question
containerlab · 9 Cisco IOS-XR (XRd) nodes on 172.20.250.0/24 · IS-IS + SR + iBGP over a route reflector
A branch off layers 2 and 5 — never in the answer path.
No model call happens unless you ask for one.
raw text withheld-with-count · free text quoted
Triggered only by: --paraphrase · analyze · agent · an MCP client
Everything else is a feature. These are the build.
lab.platform_for() reads static data only, so the
allowlist check can happen before any secret loads.
The allowlist is checked before credentials.
Ordering is load-bearing: a bad command never
reaches the network, and never costs a login.
No command is built by interpolation.
A prefix/address/name is parsed into a typed object
and the command re-rendered from its canonical form.
No unparsed device text reaches a model.
Structural, not filtered: prompt_library never holds
the text. Five egress paths, all projected.
Each is pinned by a test that fails when the guard is removed (71/71 verified).

Read down the spine: a question enters at the top, becomes an answer in layer 4, and only layers 5–7 ever touch a device. The model branch hangs off the side — it restates conclusions, it never reaches them.
